external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: The administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The CDN from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads and to which the web server publishes new assets.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server serves the public site, runs the CMS and publishes new assets to the CDN bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The content management system running on the web server.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk."

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: The CDN bucket receiving newly published images, stylesheets and downloads.

data_flows.name: hit site
data_flows.description: A reader accesses the public site on the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS
data_flows.data_description: Public site requests and responses; some readers are signed in.

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: A reader fetches images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The CMS keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Newly published images, stylesheets and downloads.

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
data_flows.notes: The connection is described as unsecured, directly to the box, with no TLS and no jump host.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server, CMS and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site that readers access.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a public site whose readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database is confidential because it contains accounts and comments, which are person-related data.
assumptions.basis: The database is stated to contain accounts and comments.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket contains public data because its images, stylesheets and downloads are fetched by readers from the public site.
assumptions.basis: The bucket receives assets that readers fetch from the CDN for the public site.
